svg.title: Hub and spoke layouts as drawn on Microsoft Learn pages, including two hub-to-hub options
svg.desc: Not an official Microsoft diagram. Five separate panels, each redrawn from a Microsoft Learn page or picture, and not one combined design. Panel A follows the Azure Architecture Center hub-spoke network topology diagram: a hub virtual network with Azure Bastion, Azure Firewall and a VPN gateway, a cross-premises network connected to the gateway, Azure Monitor receiving diagnostics, two production spokes and two nonproduction spokes each connected to the hub, forced tunnel arrows from the production spokes to the firewall, and one connection between the two nonproduction spokes. Panel B follows the Cloud Adoption Framework traditional topology diagram: three spokes each peered to one hub that holds a gateway and a firewall. Panel C follows the Azure Virtual Desktop landing zone diagram: two regional hubs peered to each other, an identity virtual network per region peered to its hub, and one Azure Virtual Desktop virtual network peered to both hubs. No spoke-to-spoke peering is drawn in panels B and C, or between the production spokes in panel A. Panel D shows hub-to-hub connection by virtual network peering between two regional hubs, from the Cloud Adoption Framework traditional topology page. Panel E shows hub-to-hub connection through ExpressRoute circuits for three regions, with no hub-to-hub peering, from the same page. D and E are separate options and are not combined.
svg.text: Hub and spoke layouts on Learn pages
Separate sources. They are options and examples, not one design.
A. Azure Architecture Center: hub-spoke network topology
Azure Virtual Network Manager (outer frame in Learn)
B. Cloud Adoption Framework: traditional topology
C. AVD landing zone design guide
Hubs hold DNS Private Resolver, gateways and Azure Firewall in Learn.
D. Cloud Adoption Framework: hub-to-hub with virtual network peering
Learn text: to connect two Azure regions, use global virtual network peering between the regional hubs.
The same Learn picture also draws ExpressRoute circuits to a customer network. They are left out here so this panel shows one option.
E. Cloud Adoption Framework: hub-to-hub through ExpressRoute (three regions)
Inbound: connection weight or AS path prepending
Panels D and E are two separate options from the same Learn page, not one design. Learn says to use peering for two regions
and to prefer shared ExpressRoute circuits for more than two. In E, hubs have no peering and spokes in other regions are reached by BGP routes.
Each panel is only what its own Learn page draws. Virtual WAN is a separate topology. Check the cited pages before copying any panel.
